text:
Maria: Hey team — quick sync. I'm thinking about leaning on gRPC for more internal service-to-service traffic (latency + contract safety). Main blocker I keep hearing: how do we keep quotas, dashboards, and rollout UX sane when methods aren't plain HTTP paths?

Ajay: +1 on gRPC for perf, but agree — our console and quota system expect a path string. gRPC has full method names like `redwood.model.Infer/Generate` which is fine but UX is noisy.

Chen: We already have an L7 gateway that maps HTTP paths -> route IDs for quotas. The mapping is central to billing and SLOs. Switching to raw gRPC would require a new mapping dimension.

Sarah: Console note: the route filter UI right now lists endpoints by path. No way to filter by proto service/method. If we change traffic shape, we'll need a consistent label to show to product owners.

Ajay: Proposal idea: keep the gRPC native wire for internal calls, but ensure the fronting layer (envoy / gateway) emits a stable route label header, e.g. `x-redwood-route: model.infer.generate:v1`. That header becomes the canonical route id for quota / console / rollouts.

Chen: That seems pragmatic. Two implementation options: (A) proto-level annotation (add an option in .proto like `(redwood.route) = "model.infer.generate:v1"`) so the grpc bridge can attach it, or (B) runtime mapping rules in the gateway that map `:method`/authority to route ids.

Sarah: I like proto annotations because the console can read a descriptor bucket and show friendly names. But shipping proto changes is slower for incremental services. Runtime mapping is faster but brittle.

Ajay: FWIW here's a tiny envoy mapping sketch I used in a spike:```yaml
- match:
    grpc_method: "redwood.model.Infer/Generate"
  apply:
    request_headers_to_add:
      - header:
          key: "x-redwood-route"
          value: "model.infer.generate:v1"
```
That attaches the label with zero payload change.

Maria: Nice. Important constraints: (1) route labels must be stable across rollouts/versions, (2) quotas should be able to be applied by label + tenant, and (3) rollout UX must show method-level success/latency for canaries.

Chen: Architecture note: if we rely on headers, ensure the header is set before any auth/authz service that uses quotas. Also consider mTLS and header spoofing — sign the header or have gateway stamp it server-side.

Ajay: We can have the gateway set `x-redwood-route` and add a signature header `x-redwood-route-sig` HMAC'd with gateway key. AuthZ can validate. Simple and effective.

Sarah: UI tasks: add a new drop-down to switch between path/method label; add an aliasing view so owners can map `model.infer.generate:v1` -> "ModelInfer.generate" for display. Also add method-level timeseries in rollouts. Low-impact front-end changes.

Maria: Action items: spike POC to prove header approach + signature + console surface. @Ajay can you take a 2d spike to wire envoy mapping -> gateway stamp -> console ingestion? Put a demo for Tuesday.

Ajay: @Maria yep. I'll open a branch `spike/grpc-route-label` and ping in this thread when there's a demo. Estimate ~16h dev + 8h to wire console ingest.

Chen: I'll sketch the quota changes (alias -> token-bucket key) and how fallback works when header missing. Wants to avoid a full rewrite of quota engine.

Sarah: I'll draft console UX mockups once Ajay has header samples. Small note: default behavior should still show human-friendly names for external teams who don't care about proto.

deploy-bot: canary started for `spike/grpc-route-label` env test cluster (test-01). Logs: `envoy: header x-redwood-route set for 3 services`

Maria: Great. After spike, decide proto-annotation vs runtime mapping. Proto-annotation wins for long-term stability, but runtime mapping wins for speed. POC should surface operational tradeoffs.

Ajay: Also adding: need to consider SDKs — some SDKs call via JSON-over-HTTP to gateway, others use gRPC directly. We should define the canonical route id generation algorithm so both sides converge.

Chen: Agreed. I'll draft a short RFC after spike: mapping rules, signature semantics, quota compatibility.

Sarah: :thumbsup: Thanks all — this feels actionable.

Maria: Thanks — ping me when demo is up.
